data.name: Nathanael
data.gender_notes: Nathanael is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Hebrew, Nathanael means 'given by God'. In the New Testament, Nathanael is a disciple of Jesus. The name Nathanael carries the meaning “Given by God” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Nathanael usually hope their child will grow to embody given by god and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolic of divine guidance and revelation.
data.etymology: Nathanael belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Given by God.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Nathanael total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

in_hebrew.name: נָתָנָאֵל
in_hebrew.long_meaning: נָתָנָאֵל הוא שם עברי שמשמעו מתנה מאלוהים, והוא מורכב משני חלקים: נתן שפירושו מתנה, ואל שהוא שם האלוהים. השם נָתָנָאֵל מופיע בברית החדשה כאחד מתלמידיו של ישו.

in_greek.name: Ναθαναήλ
in_greek.long_meaning: Ναθαναήλ ἐστιν ὄνομα Ἑβραϊκὸν τὸ σημαῖνον δώρον παρὰ θεοῦ, καὶ συνθέτουν δύο μέρη: Ναθαν τὸ σημαῖνον δώρον, καὶ Ἠλ τὸ ὄνομα τοῦ Θεοῦ. Τὸ ὄνομα Ναθαναήλ ἀναφέρεται ἐν τῇ Καινῇ Διαθήκῃ ὡς ἕνας τῶν μαθητῶν τοῦ Ἰησοῦ.

in_latin.name: Nathanael
in_latin.long_meaning: Nathanael est nomen Hebraicum significans Dei donum, et constat ex duobus partibus: Nathan, quod significat donum, et El, quod est nomen Dei. Nomen Nathanael in Nova Testamenta mentionem habet ut unus ex discipulis Iesu.

in_english.name: Nathanael
in_english.long_meaning: Nathanael is a Hebrew name meaning Gift of God, derived from two parts: Nathan, meaning gift, and El, referring to God. The name Nathanael appears in the New Testament as one of Jesus' disciples, symbolizing spiritual gift and divine favor.

data.cultural_impact: Nathanael is a biblical name of deep historical and cultural significance. Named after the ancient Hebrew prophet Nathan, who played a crucial role in the establishment and preservation of the Jewish monarchy, the name Nathanael represents a connection to the rich history of the Jewish people and their faith. The name also evokes images of the ancient Middle Eastern world and the powerful religious traditions that emerged from that region.
data.spiritual_significance: The meaning of the name Nathanael, 'given by God', holds immense spiritual significance for Christians. It reminds us that every human being is a unique gift from God, created in His image and loved unconditionally. Furthermore, the life of the biblical Nathanael, as recorded in the New Testament, serves as a powerful reminder of the transformative power of God's grace. Despite Nathanael's initial skepticism and doubt, Jesus saw the potential in him and called him to be a disciple, ultimately leading him to become a key figure in the early Christian community. The name Nathanael, therefore, stands as a reminder of the power of God's grace to transform even the most ordinary lives into something extraordinary.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Nathanael, meaning "given by God," symbolizes the belief that God chooses and blesses those whom He calls for a special purpose. It is a reminder of God's sovereignty and faithfulness in selecting and equipping His servants for divine missions.

biblical_reference.note: Nathanael is mentioned as a disciple of Jesus, introduced by Philip, and recognized by Jesus as an Israelite without deceit.

historical_references.reference: Nathanael is identified as a disciple of Jesus Christ in the New Testament, specifically in the Gospel of John (1:45-51). He is introduced as a man from Cana in Galilee, and is described as being introduced to Jesus by Philip.
historical_references.context: An account of Nathanael's encounter with Jesus, recorded in the Gospel of John.

historical_references.reference: Nathanael is also mentioned in the Synoptic Gospels (Matthew 10:3; Mark 3:18; Luke 6:14) as one of the Twelve Apostles, but his origin is not specified there.
historical_references.context: Lists of the apostles found in the Synoptic Gospels.

modern_usage.modern_context: Nathanael is a name of Hebrew origin, meaning 'given by God'. It is a modern and unique name with a nostalgic feel, popular among those who appreciate biblical names. Nathanael is seen on various platforms including social media, where it is used as a unique handle or username. Baby names websites feature Nathanael as a trending name for new parents looking for unique, biblical names for their children. Nathanael is also seen in literature and media, such as in the popular novel 'The Book Thief' by Markus Zusak, where the character Nathanael Maximilian Marcus Moser is a significant character.

name_in_real_life.story: Sarah Nathanael from Dublin, Ireland embodies the meaning of Nathanael - "Given by God". Raised in a Christian family, they were taught to honor the significance of their name and walk in faith throughout their life.
